title: Workflow Automation Custom Roles: Plans Compared
summary: Workflow automation custom roles let you define permissions your way. See which platforms support them and how they differ in functionality.
body_markdown:
## Platform-by-platform Notes on Roles and Limits


Where I give no role name, plan or price, treat it as unconfirmed and therefore a no; each entry below records only what a vendor's own documentation can settle.


I haven't printed page URLs or check dates here, because an entry without a page you opened yourself is a claim you can't audit.


Write the address and the date you read it beside each entry before you rely on it.


### Zapier roles and plan limits


Open the help-center article on team and member permissions and the pricing page. Quote the role names verbatim, then note which plan the permissions article attaches them to.


If the page names only fixed roles, custom roles don't exist on that plan, so the main limit to test is whether you can define your own role or only assign fixed ones. Choose Zapier if fixed roles already match your approval chain.


### Make roles and plan limits


Read the roles page and the pricing page together, and ask whether you can edit any role or only assign it; Make's documentation describes access at organization and team level.


Fixed roles that cover your separation of duties are enough. If they don't, you're asking for something the page doesn't state, and the answer is a sales conversation.


### n8n roles and plan limits


Of all the entries, n8n is the one where self-hosting changes the answer. Read the documentation on user roles and ask a pointed question: are the role features in the free self-hosted build, or do they need a licensed edition with a key?


Ask for the license text and read the clause that gates the feature. Choose n8n only after that clause confirms your deployment, not the vendor's cloud, receives the roles.


### Workato roles and plan limits


According to its documentation, Workato offers role-based access with configurable collaborator roles. The main limit is commercial: Workato quotes its pricing rather than listing it, so the plan that unlocks custom roles is whatever your order form says.


Ask for the role entitlement as a named line in the contract. Choose Workato if you need granular roles and accept a quoted price. If the paper lacks the line, you've bought nothing.


### Power Automate roles and limits


Under Microsoft's environment model, security roles on the environment govern access to Power Automate, rather than the automation product alone. Read Microsoft's security-role documentation and the licensing guide, and confirm which license the environment requires.


Test for dependency: custom roles may require a licensed environment, not the per-user plan you priced. Choose it if your organization already administers those environments.
